newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Hedging in T-bonds before jobs report.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Hedging in T-bonds before jobs report.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond market participants hedged up positions in options to prepare for Friday's July employment data, floor traders said.
The focus early in the session Thursday was on buying puts and put spreads in September, and buying out-of-the-money calls in December primarily in the 118-00, 120-00 and 122-00 strikes, they said.
The call buying most likely was mortgage-related hedging as insurance against a sharp rally in bonds following Friday's numbers, said one options broker.
Those who bought puts may have been hedging long futures positions or establishing short positions in expectation of a pullback in bonds, the broker said.

Implied volatilities for bond options were essentially unchanged for most of the session, ending at around 8.2 percent in September and 8.6 percent in December, floor brokers said. September went out near where it opened after dipping slightly intraday.
In the underlying futures, September bonds settled up 12/32 at 116-24/32 after reaching another new high in the steep upturn that began in April.
September bond futures are at their highest point in 1-1/2 years.
Options traders said the bulk of the day's activity began to wind down mid-morning as participants wrapped up business in preparation for Friday's key event.

July nonfarm payrolls are predicted to rise 193,000, compared with June's 217,000 increase, according to a Reuters poll of economists. The unemployment rate is seen slipping back to 4.9 percent from 5.0 percent.

Also due out Friday are June U.S. personal income and consumption data, June factory orders, the National Association of Purchasing Management business barometer and the University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey.
Eurodollar traders said put buying was also featured in the short end, with one brokerage house alone purchasing 5,000 March 93.75 puts.
Volatility rates were steady to higher after front-end values fell earlier this week. September rose 0.5 percentage point to 7.0 percent and December was unchanged at 10.0 percent.
